title: He was getting rich from broken people…
paragraphs: He was getting rich from broken people…
Because this story will either offend your pride…

He wasn’t praying.
He wasn’t repenting.
He wasn’t “trying to be better.”
He was sitting in a tax booth—counting coins that came from the pain of others.

That quiet ache.
That silent accusation.
That voice that whispers at night—
“This isn’t who you were meant to be.”
Sin pays… until it costs your soul.

No announcement.
No thunder.
No warning.
And with one sentence, everything shifts:

No lecture.
No conditions.
No “fix yourself first.”
Why would a holy Savior call a corrupt man?

Why would purity step into filth…
and not step back?
Because Jesus sees deeper than reputation.
And He didn’t come to admire good people.
He came to rescue bound ones.
Levi had built his life on a lie.
And Jesus didn’t decorate that lie—
He demolished it with an invitation.
“And leaving everything, he rose and followed him.” (Luke 5:28)
Because this is where many admire Jesus…
but stop short of following Him.
but we also want the booth.

The secret habit.
The hidden compromise.
The sin that still pays us in comfort.
Some of us are still sitting at tables Jesus already called us out of.
Still collecting what is killing us.

Still smiling in public…
while rotting in private.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
Sin is not just what we do.
It’s what we are without Christ—
and still be far from God.
They saw Levi and were disgusted.
They saw Jesus with sinners—and were offended.
“Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?” (Luke 5:30)
“Why are You near people like that?”
“Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I have not come to call the righteous but sinners to repentance.” (Luke 5:31–32)
Jesus didn’t come for the self-righteous.
Not those who pretend they’re fine—
but those who know they’re not.
Some scholars interpret this as Jesus confronting false righteousness—the illusion that external obedience equals internal purity.
You don’t need a Savior if you think you’re already good.
But if you know you’re sick…
And here is the Gospel—clear and unfiltered:
You are more sinful than you want to admit…
but more loved than you can imagine.
And the cost of sin is not small:
“For the wages of sin is death…” (Romans 6:23)
That’s the booth we all sit in.
But the verse doesn’t end there:
“…but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” (Romans 6:23)
He came to pay for Levi.
At the cross, Christ took the penalty of sin.
“God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
While we were still sitting at the booth.

Still guilty.
Still compromised.
Still undeserving.
He didn’t wait for you to change.

proving sin doesn’t win,
death doesn’t win,
shame doesn’t win.
He didn’t say, “Let me slowly transition.”
What are you holding onto that Jesus is calling you to leave?

That relationship?
That habit?
That secret?
That identity?
That’s not guilt trying to crush you.
That’s grace trying to wake you up.
Because Jesus is still walking into booths.

Turn from sin.
Trust in Christ.
Surrender your life.
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
Don’t silence the voice that is trying to rescue you.
“Jesus, I’m getting up. I leave my sin. I trust Your cross. I surrender my life. Lead me. Save me. Change me.”
If this stirred something in you…
